incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED: Elevated container restarts on gpu-pool-3 (prefill path). Auto-pager triggered. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1719876543

ajay (oncall): paging @maria @linh — seeing a spike in OOM-related container restarts, prefill path specifically. taking initial triage. :pager:

maria (sre): noticed restart spike at 2024-10-18T10:02:00Z. Node 'gpu-3b' shows repeated kubelet evictions. Restarts correlate with requests that have very large prompt lengths.

linh (runtime): logs from one crashed container (short) — looks like CUDA OOM during prefill KV allocation. not seeing a model image rollout in deploy history right now.
```
[2024-10-18T10:02:11Z] runtime.ERROR prefill_worker.py:234 allocate_kv_cache failed: RuntimeError('CUDA out of memory.')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/prefill_worker.py\", line 232, in process_prefill
    kv_cache = allocate_kv(device, required_bytes)
  File \"/app/memory.py\", line 45, in allocate_kv
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory.
[2024-10-18T10:02:13Z] system INFO containerd: oom_kill: process restarted (exit code 137)
```

sarah (support): impact: 3 active customers reporting errors via support (acme-beta, lumen-ai, chatly). Error spike shows 5xx rate up ~0.8% cluster-wide, but for affected routes it's ~8-12%.

kyle (cs): acme-beta on call: their jobs time out and get 502, they started a support thread. they're asking for ETA. I've opened a customer incident and flagged it critical.

deploy-bot: No active deploys in the last 6 hours to runtime images. Canary jobs passed earlier today (no changes to prefill code).

ajay (oncall): proposed quick mitigations: 1) disable prefill for long-context requests (> 8192 tokens) at the routing layer 2) route traffic for heavy-context customers to 'redwood-slim' (smaller kv footprint) 3) patch PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS env to 4096 on gpu-pool-3. Who can apply?

linh (runtime): I can push the hotpatch. Recommend PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096 and PREFILL_BATCH_LIMIT=8 first. Also enable PREFILL_FAIL_SAFE=true to fall back to streaming prefill instead of all-at-once for big requests. Quick patch command (internal):
```bash
# update runtime config via control plane API
curl -X POST \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://control-plane.internal/runtime/pools/gpu-pool-3/config \
  -d '{"env": {"PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS": "4096", "PREFILL_BATCH_LIMIT": "8", "PREFILL_FAIL_SAFE": "true"}}'
```

maria (sre): I'm going to cordon + drain the most-affected nodes to force a rolling restart after the env change. I'll also temporarily increase the scheduler's prefill backpressure threshold to avoid very large concurrent prefill jobs. Starting now.

maria (sre): applied env patch, rolling restart initiated on gpu-pool-3. patch applied at 2024-10-18T10:08:45Z.

linh (runtime): confirm: runtime config accepted. Instances will pick up new env on restart. Also kicked a canary: sent 20 long-context requests — prefill now falls back to streaming mode instead of allocating full KV: no OOM in canary.

maria (sre): after restart, restart-rate dropped to baseline within 4 minutes on the patched nodes. Monitoring dashboard: container restarts per minute down from 7 -> 0.8.

ajay (oncall): good. rerouting heavy customers to redwood-slim now. @kyle can you tell acme-beta we applied a mitigation and will follow up with RCA?

kyle (cs): on it — pinged acme-beta support contact, they want a postmortem email. noted.

sarah (support): updating status page: brief note that some requests were affected and that mitigation is in progress. :white_check_mark:

linh (runtime): observed error logs post-patch — a few residual OOMs due to inflight requests started before the change, otherwise good. Example trace shows fallback path executed:
```
[2024-10-18T10:11:02Z] runtime.INFO prefill: detected large request (token_est=12000), using streaming_prefill fallback.
[2024-10-18T10:11:05Z] runtime.INFO prefill: streaming_prefill completed for request id=abc123, peak_gpu_mem=7.2GB
```

maria (sre): rolling restart finished. Marking affected nodes as schedulable and watching for 30m. Alerts silenced for the specific incident alert group.

ajay (oncall): handoff summary for next oncall (maria will own):
- root cause: large-context prefill allocations causing CUDA OOMs and container restarts on gpu-pool-3 when concurrent long-prefill requests spike.
- mitigation applied: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=4096, PREFILL_BATCH_LIMIT=8, PREFILL_FAIL_SAFE=true, route heavy customers to redwood-slim, drained + restarted affected nodes.
- impact: 3 customers reported, cluster 5xx rate +0.8% for ~12 minutes, affected routes saw 8-12% 5xx for ~10 minutes. No data loss.
- next actions (tickets created):
  * RUNTIME-4721: implement model-level prefill safety checks and prefill admission control.
  * OBS-1983: alert for prefill OOM count + automatic temporary throttling.
  * CS-889: customer communication / postmortem for acme-beta, lumen-ai, chatly.

maria (sre): taking oncall handoff. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate if any regressions. If you need me, DM.

ajay (oncall): thanks team — closing pager for now. :thumbsup: follow-up notes and RCA to be drafted in 24h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 2024-10-18T10:18:50Z — all core symptoms mitigated. Full postmortem ID: PM-2024-10-prefill-oom-1719876543 (to be published after review).

kyle (cs): noted for customer updates. will include mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fixes.

linh (runtime): will open a follow-up PR to add prefill token budgeting and an integration test for long-context requests.

maria (sre): final check: error rate stable, no new OOMs in the last 12 minutes. handoff complete.

ajay (oncall): last note — we should add a synthetic job that exercises edge-case long prefill to catch regressions in CI. filing OBS ticket now.
